patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher in her late twenties who joined in 2024 with recurrent cystitis; two culture-positive E. coli episodes treated here, then bacterial vaginosis twice at an outside gynecology office whose notes arrive late.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 27 y/o woman looking for a new primary care doctor. Her old office stopped taking her plan's tier after the school district switched carriers. Explained membership and the fee schedule; she wants to enroll. Booked new patient visit Tue 9/10 at 3:45 (after school). Sent intake forms and the records release for her prior PCP office through the portal.

conditions.label: Recurrent urinary tract infections
conditions.note: several episodes over the past few years; most recent April 2024, treated at an urgent care

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 27 y/o F, teaches second grade. Here to establish; feels well.

Main issue she wants on the radar: bladder infections. Has had them on and off for several years, a few a year at worst. Most recent was in April, seen at an urgent care, given a short course of an antibiotic she can't name; cleared. No hx of fevers, flank pain or hospitalization with any of them. No kidney stones. Mother has had the same problem for years.

PMH: recurrent UTIs, otherwise none.
PSH: tonsils out at age 8.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FHx: mother with recurrent UTIs; father with high blood pressure.
Social: never smoked. A drink or two a month. One partner, condoms some of the time. Lives locally, teaches at an elementary school.
Gyn: periods regular. Last Pap 2023 at her old office, told normal.
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal, tonsillar pillars surgically absent. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. Skin clear. Mood and affect normal.

A/P
1. Recurrent UTIs, by history. Discussed fluids and voiding after intercourse. If symptoms start, message or call and we'll see her same day with a urine sample rather than treating blind.
2. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP and lipids; one-time HIV and hep C screening today. Requesting records from prior PCP office (release signed). Pap next due 2026. Flu and COVID boosters once the fall supply is in.
RTC: annual, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Isabelle, everything from Tuesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol all fine, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received by fax, 14 pages, from the patient's previous primary care office (care 2016 to 2024).

Summary of contents: annual visits, unremarkable. Problem list: recurrent cystitis. Surgical history: tonsillectomy in childhood. Medications: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Cervical cytology 2023: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
Immunizations: childhood series complete per state registry printout; HPV series complete; Tdap 2009; influenza most years; COVID primary series 2021.
Several urine cultures in past years listed by date only; reports not included.

Scanned to chart. Reviewed by PCP.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for seasonal vaccines. Afebrile, no current illness, no prior vaccine reactions. Influenza (trivalent) IM left deltoid, COVID-19 updated mRNA IM right deltoid. VIS given. Observed 15 min, tolerated well. Left after.

documents.title: Burning again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - I think I have another UTI. Burning when I pee and going constantly since yesterday afternoon. No fever. I can come in after 3 today if there's a spot, otherwise I'll try to get coverage for my class.

documents.title: RE: Burning again
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Good morning, we have a 3:20 today with the doctor. Please bring yourself in without emptying your bladder right before, we'll need a sample. Push fluids in the meantime.

medications.drug: nitrofurantoin, macrocrystals 25 MG / nitrofurantoin, monohydrate 75 MG Oral Capsule
medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily with food for 5 days

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Dysuria and frequency starting yesterday afternoon. Mild urgency. No fever, chills, back or flank pain, nausea. No discharge or genital sores. No new partner. First episode since April.

O: Afebrile, vitals as charted. Comfortable. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft, mild discomfort low midline only with deep palpation.
UA (in office): LE 1+, nitrite positive, blood negative; micro WBC 20/hpf, RBC 0/hpf, many bacteria. Culture sent.

A/P: Uncomplicated cystitis, second documented episode this year counting April.
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x 5 days with food.
- Will call with culture. If fever, flank pain or not better in 48h, let us know.
- Reviewed voiding after sex and hydration again.

documents.title: Urine culture result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Isabelle - your urine culture grew E. coli, and it's sensitive to the nitrofurantoin you're on, so just finish the five days. Hope you're already feeling better.

documents.title: RE: Urine culture result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: All better by day 2, finished the pills Saturday. Thank you for squeezing me in!

documents.title: Same-day request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling before work. Two days of burning, frequency and lower belly ache, says it feels exactly like November. No fever, no back pain, no vomiting. Not pregnant per pt, period was a couple weeks ago. Offered 12:40 (her lunch block); accepted. Asked her to bring a urine sample or come in able to give one.

documents.title: Acute Visit - Urinary Symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o F with recurrent UTIs.

HPI: Since Saturday, painful urination, frequency and a dull ache above the pubic bone. By her count this is the third bout in about a year: April (urgent care), November here (culture E. coli, treated with nitrofurantoin), and now. No fever, rigors or flank pain. Denies discharge, genital lesions, or any new partner; same partner, condoms used inconsistently. LMP about two weeks ago, normal.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: vitals normal (see flowsheet). Nontoxic. Abdomen soft, tender suprapubically, no rebound. No CVA tenderness.

UA today: LE 2+, nitrite +, blood neg; WBC 35/hpf, RBC 2/hpf, many bacteria.

Assessment: acute cystitis, recurrent pattern. Prior culture E. coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin.

Plan:
- Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily x 5 days.
- Urine culture sent; will adjust if resistant.
- Hydration, void after intercourse.
- Call for fever, flank pain, vomiting, or no improvement in 2 days.

documents.title: Culture back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Culture grew E. coli again, sensitive to what you're taking. Keep going through the full course. How are the symptoms?

documents.title: RE: Culture back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Totally fine now, done with the antibiotic yesterday. Thanks.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it time for my yearly checkup? Kids come back next week so anything after 3:15 works best.

documents.title: RE: Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Yes, you're due. You're booked Monday 9/8 at 3:30. No fasting needed.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. 28 y/o teacher, school year just started, feels good.

Interval: no UTIs since the February episode. No urinary symptoms now. No other illnesses, no ED or urgent care visits.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social unchanged: never smoker, 1-2 drinks a month, same partner.
PHQ-2 = 0.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: BP and vitals on flowsheet, normal. Weight steady. Eyes, ears, throat normal. No lymphadenopathy, thyroid normal. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities normal. Skin: no worrisome lesions. Neuro grossly intact.

Assessment and plan:
- Recurrent UTIs: quiet since February. Same-day visits with a urine sample remain the plan if symptoms recur.
- Last Tdap 2009 per old records: Tdap given today.
- Pap from 2023 normal, due next year.
- Labs from last fall all normal; nothing needed today.
- Flu and COVID vaccines in October at a nurse visit.
Follow up next year.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days

documents.title: External fill history
documents.author: MA
documents.body: External prescription history import flagged a new fill: metronidazole 500 mg tablets, #14, 1 tab twice daily, filled 10/13/2025. Prescriber is an outside gynecologist. No visit note from that office on file. Added to med list as an outside short course; routing to PCP.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Here for flu and updated COVID shots. Feels well, afebrile. Asked about the metronidazole that showed up on her fill history: she went to her gynecologist last week for discharge with an odor and was told it was a bacterial imbalance (BV). Finished the 7 days yesterday, avoided alcohol while on it, symptoms gone. No urinary symptoms.

Flu (trivalent) IM L deltoid, COVID-19 updated mRNA IM R deltoid. VIS reviewed. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction.

Records request faxed to the gynecology office for the 10/13 visit.

documents.title: Records request follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called the gynecology office about our 10/21 records request. Their records person said it's in the queue; re-faxed the signed release at their request. Will check again.

documents.title: Gynecology office visit 10/13/2025
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP - OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 10/13/2025
Patient: Isabelle Beaulieu, 28 y/o

Reason for visit: vaginal discharge x 1 week.

History: Notes a thin, white discharge for about a week with a pronounced fishy smell, more noticeable after sex. No itching, no burning. Hx recurrent bladder infections, most recently cystitis in February treated by her PCP. Currently on no medications. NKDA. Monogamous, condoms used inconsistently.

Exam: External genitalia normal, no erythema or swelling of the vulva. Speculum: homogeneous white discharge adherent to the vaginal walls. Cervix normal appearing.

Office testing: pH 5.0. Amine (whiff) test positive. Saline wet prep with clue cells.

Impression: bacterial vaginosis.

Plan: metronidazole 500 mg PO BID x 7 days; no alcohol during treatment and for 3 days after. Return if symptoms persist.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Gynecology office visit 06/01/2026
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY GROUP - OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 06/01/2026
Patient: Isabelle Beaulieu, 29 y/o

CC: discharge with odor, one week.

HPI: Returns with grayish-white discharge and a fishy smell for the past week, again worse after intercourse. Similar to her BV last October. Denies itching, burning or painful urination. LMP 2 weeks ago.

PMH: recurrent UTIs; acute cystitis 2025; bacterial vaginosis 10/2025.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: one partner, inconsistent condom use.

Exam: Vulva without erythema or edema. Speculum: thin gray discharge pooled in the vaginal vault. Bimanual: no cervical motion tenderness.

Microscopy: clue cells present (squamous cells with stippled, bacteria-coated borders). Vaginal pH 5.5.

Assessment: bacterial vaginosis, recurrent.

Plan: metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days, avoid alcohol. Follow up as needed.

Prior note from 10/13/2025 enclosed per your request.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days

reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summer break, in to catch up and get her Pap done.

Reviewed the gynecology notes that came in on 6/12: BV in October 2025 (pH 5.0, whiff positive, clue cells) and again 6/1/2026 (pH 5.5, clue cells), metronidazole 7 days both times. She finished the June course and the discharge cleared. Adding BV to her problem list; it wasn't put on after the October visit.

Urinary: no cystitis since February 2025. No dysuria or frequency now.

Meds: none current. NKDA. Social unchanged.

Exam: vitals normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: external genitalia normal, normal vaginal mucosa, no discharge today, cervix without lesions. Pap collected.

A/P
1. Bacterial vaginosis, twice in 8 months, treated by her gynecologist; resolved for now. She'll go back to them if it returns.
2. Recurrent UTIs, quiet for over a year. Same plan for symptoms.
3. Cervical screening: cytology sent today; result by portal.
Physical in September.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Isabelle, your Pap came back normal. Next one in three years. Enjoy the rest of the summer.

documents.title: RE: Pap result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great news, thank you!
